paper.title_en: Perturbative construction of amplitudes from on-shell trees with vacuum pairs: the all-plus four-gluon amplitude through order $g^6$
paper.abstract_en: We formulate a systematic on-shell construction of perturbative amplitudes by combining the Feynman-tree theorem with BCFW recursion. Amplitudes are built entirely from on-shell tree amplitudes generated by BCFW and are supplemented by additional unobservable state-conjugate on-shell pairs, called vacuum pairs, whose momenta are integrated over Lorentz-invariant phase space. At fixed coupling order, the contributing tree amplitudes are classified by polygon bookkeeping, while their products form forests whose relative signs are fixed by inclusion-exclusion. We show that these signs coincide with the signs assigned by the full Feynman-tree-theorem cut expansion, so that the construction reproduces the ordinary perturbative loop expansion order by order. The dynamical tree input consists of the allowed three-point on-shell amplitudes; the particle spectrum, couplings, and color data are taken as given, and no off-shell object is introduced at any stage. As a nontrivial test of this equivalence, we study the four-gluon all-plus amplitude through orders $g^4$ and $g^6$. The on-shell construction reproduces the finite rational one-loop primitive amplitude and the known bare planar and non-planar two-loop primitive integrands, including the bow-tie terms in the planar primitive.
